summary.text: Lori Trahan is the incumbent for Massachusetts's 3rd District, serving since 2019.
A Lowell native and Georgetown graduate, she worked for Rep. Marty Meehan, rising to chief of staff, before a private-sector career as a tech-company executive and consulting-firm co-founder.
She sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and holds House Democratic leadership roles.

paragraphs.text: Trahan was born in Lowell, Massachusetts, in 1973; according to her official biography, she is the granddaughter of immigrants and grew up in a working-class family, her father a union ironworker.
She graduated from Lowell Public Schools and Lowell High School, then attended Georgetown University on a volleyball scholarship, according to her official biography.
She earned a bachelor's degree in regional and comparative studies in 1995 and says she was the first in her family to graduate from college.
After college Trahan joined the staff of then-Rep. Marty Meehan (D), rising to chief of staff.

After about a decade in public service she moved to the private sector as an executive at an early-stage tech firm, then co-founded a women-owned consulting firm and served as CEO of the Concire Leadership Institute.
Trahan ran for Congress in 2018, her first campaign for public office, and took office in January 2019.

She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and, in House Democratic leadership, as Co-Chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee, Senior Whip, and a member of the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee, per her official biography.
Her office credits her with securing passage of the Leonel Rondon Pipeline Safety Act after the Merrimack Valley gas explosions and with co-founding the Pandemic Preparedness Caucus.
According to her official biography, she lives in the district with her husband, Dave, and their two daughters.
